STEP 1 - Scene: A snack of whole roasted/raw almonds (shelled, brown skins) on a small plate. No other dishes in the meal area; a small orange fragment sits at the upper right of the plate.

STEP 2 - Vessel: A square white plate, roughly 20 cm across. Area ≈ 314 cm² (using the inscribed round approximation for a 20 cm plate).

STEP 3 - Items:
- Almonds (about 22 whole nuts)
- A tiny orange piece (carrot or similar), negligible
- A tiny yellow fleck near the lower right edge, negligible

STEP 4 - Area: The almond cluster covers roughly a 110–120 cm² footprint in the center, about 35% of the vessel area. Almonds are mostly in a single layer with some overlap, so food coverage is about 35%. The orange fragment and yellow fleck are under 1% combined.

STEP 5 - Volume: Almond pile footprint ≈ 115 cm², typical height ≈ 1.2 cm (two layers in places, mostly one). Gross volume ≈ 115 × 1.2 ≈ 138 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Whole almonds have a bulk density around 0.5–0.6 g/ml (they are irregular and leave gaps). Using 0.55 g/ml: 138 × 0.55 ≈ 76 g. Cross-check: 22 almonds at about 1.2 g each ≈ 26 g, which is well below 76 g, so the volume estimate is probably high. Taking the count-based estimate as more reliable, and allowing for the apparent 2-layer areas, I settle on about 30 g of almonds. The orange and yellow bits add under 1 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Raw/roasted almonds ≈ 579 kcal/100 g (dry, shelled). 30 g × 5.79 ≈ 174 kcal. The carrot-like bit adds about 1 kcal, so the total is roughly 175 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: About 22 almonds is a typical small handful (about 30 g, roughly 170 kcal), which fits a plate that is only about a third covered. Plausible.

Total: about 30 g, about 175 kcal.
